findings.title: Date-override unavailable-day check uses reference equality and never matches
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable compares two newly created Dayjs objects with ===. Two different objects are never ===, so the empty-override (start == end means day is unavailable) branch never returns true. Because dateOverrideExist is still set to true, execution falls through to if (dateOverrideExist) return true, marking slots on an unavailable day as available and allowing booking when the host blocked the whole day.

findings.title: Working-hours end check ignores event length
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable computes both start and end as slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute(). The slot end time (start + eventLength) is never used. A slot starting inside working hours but ending outside (e.g. 30-min slot at 17:45 with hours ending at 18:00 for a 60-min event) is treated as inside, so events can be booked past the end of working hours.

findings.title: Split working hours incorrectly marked unavailable
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find(h => outside) to reject a slot. When a user has two intervals on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a slot at 10:00 is inside the first interval but outside the second, so find returns the second interval and the slot is rejected as outside working hours. Correct logic must accept if ANY interval for that day contains the slot, not reject if ANY interval does not contain it.

findings.title: Date-override day matching uses server-local time and wrong date basis
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable computes utcOffset from organizerTimeZone then does dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD') compared to slotStartTime.format where slotStartTime is UTC. dayjs(date.start) without tz renders in the server local timezone, so the result depends on where the server runs, and the comparison is against UTC date instead of organizer-local date. An override at 00:30 organizer time (previous-day UTC) is attributed to the wrong calendar day, causing overrides to be ignored or applied to the wrong day.

findings.title: Date-override timezone shift crashes on missing timezone and drops midnight crossover
findings.body: In packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots does dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset() where TimeRange.timeZone is optional. When undefined, tz(undefined) throws/misbehaves. It also parses via toString() instead of the Date instant, uses only the start instant offset for both start and end, and reduces to hour()*60+minute. An override that shifts across midnight in invitee timezone (e.g. 00:30 organizer becomes previous/next day invitee) loses the day component and is placed on the wrong invitee day, and overrides spanning midnight get start > end and produce no slots.
